title: fix(sdui-parser): keep the boundary space between a text run and a sibling element
body:
Fixes #11148 ## What was wrong `parseChildren` (`packages/sdui-parser/src/parse.ts`) collapsed each text run's whitespace to a single space — correct, that is HTML's own whitespace model — and then `.trim()`ed it, which is not: HTML collapses a whitespace run to one space, it does not delete it. What the trim deleted is exactly the space separating a text run from an adjacent sibling element, so this source ```jsx

A x page

``` parsed to `['A', {strong}, 'page']` and the words run together wherever that tree is rendered. The line was re-derived at `origin/main` `a872ce9` before any edit and was still where the card names it (`parse.ts:168`). ## The rule applied — triage ruling, option (b), adopted verbatim Collapse the run, then keep **one leading space when a sibling precedes** the run and **one trailing space when a sibling element follows** it; at the parent's own start/end the edge space is still dropped, so a paragraph authored with padding around `Hello` still compiles to `['Hello']`. It is deliberately mechanical — it invents no block/inline taxonomy for a schema tree that has none (the rejected option (a)). ## The rule's known cost, pinned rather than argued A whitespace-only run **between two siblings** survives as a single space, so a pretty-printed list gains one `' '` string child per inter-item gap. That bound is the required control in the test file, asserted as the thing that could have gone wrong: exactly one single-space child per gap, never the source's newline plus indentation, never at the container's own edges, and never inside an item's own text. ## Not a cherry-pick The downstream copy of this parser landed the same ruling first, but the two files have drifted (the downstream one carries an html-tier provenance stamp: one import, an eight-line comment and a marking call), so the line numbers differ and are expected to keep differing. The patch here is written against **this** tree; what the two copies share is the **behaviour**, which is what the new tests pin. ## Non-vacuity — the tests fail on the unfixed parser Written before the fix and run against it: ``` Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 7 failed | 1 passed (8) ``` The single pre-fix pass is the parent-edge control (`still drops the edge space at the parent's own start and end`) — the half of `.trim()` that was correct, and which must stay green in both directions. The list-bound control fails before the fix too (`Full HTML tag set in thehtmltier.`), which is what makes it a pin rather than a restatement. ## Blast radius, re-measured on today's tree The card graded this contract drift rather than a user-visible bug on the claim that the one in-tree consumer's findings do not depend on the whitespace — measured on a different tree (`acb4dbc`). Re-measured here at `a872ce9`: - Repo-wide sweep for importers of the package: **exactly one** source file, `packages/lint/src/validate-jsx-pages.ts`, which reads `diagnostics` only and never the tree. (`packages/cli/src/utils/sdui-manifest.ts` and the `packages/spec` matches name it in comments only.) - No fixture or snapshot in `packages/lint` encodes the trimmed shape: its suite is green unchanged against the rebuilt parser — 80 files, 2246 passed, 5 skipped. - The claim holds. No file outside `packages/sdui-parser` is touched by this PR. ## Verification — all at `edc48fc`, the head of this branch | command | result | | --- | --- | | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/sdui-parser test --maxWorkers=2` | `Test Files 2 passed (2)` · `Tests 14 passed (14)` | | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/sdui-parser typecheck` | clean | | `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test --maxWorkers=2` | `Test Files 80 passed (80)` · `Tests 2246 passed, 5 skipped (2251)` | | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` | clean | | `eslint . --no-inline-config` (whole repo, not narrowed) | 4979 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings | Gate families derived from the actual changed paths with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (12 path-matched plus 6 convention-triggered by adding a test file) — all green at `edc48fc`: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:published-files`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape`, `check-affected-docs`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:where-matcher`. One declared narrowing: `check:type-check-debt` (`--re-measure`) needs the whole `packages/*` closure built. `@objectstack/sdui-parser` carries no ledger entry at all (its own `typecheck` covers it, run above), and the only ledger entry this diff can reach is `@objectstack/lint`, the sole importer — measured directly with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`, clean. The diff moves no type or signature, only statement-level behaviour. ## Changeset `patch` on `@objectstack/sdui-parser`: output values move, no API changes, no input's acceptance changes. `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset` both agree (`This diff introduces no major bump`; `No empty-frontmatter changeset introduced`). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx)_
